neighbours.label: ' today' or ' Today' setting the present against a past just described ('rebuilt in the thirteenth century, and today', 'still endures today'); ' today' as this calendar day stays low.
fire: The custom began under the Romans and survives even in Sicily today.
That old quarrel over land matters in today's politics.
The abbey burned in the twelfth century, and today its walls stand open.
The tribe once ruled the valley. Today, few speak its language.
Built by monks long ago, the bridge is still in use today.
Medieval guilds set the rules, and today their halls are museums.
This medieval law bears on today's debate.
The town was a Viking port, and today it sells souvenirs.
quiet: My sister phoned me and asked to meet in Sicily today.
That dentist appointment was moved to today's last slot.
The mail came at noon, and today my box was full.
The bus was late. Today, I walked to work.
Built by monks long ago, the bridge is closed for repairs today.
Our lunch got cancelled, and today we ate at our desks.
The shop is closed, and today it rained.

notes: Probes: 0.58-0.74 for ' today' after a historical lead-in, 'Today,' 0.29, 'Even today' 0.12; calendar 'today' 0.01-0.06.
